takeaway: Small cell (oat-cell) carcinoma is highly malignant, metastasises early and is often associated with ectopic hormone production and paraneoplastic syndromes, such as hypercalcaemia.

lines.text: A fifty-two year old woman has a rapidly worsening cough, haemoptysis, and breathlessness at rest.
Her chest radiograph shows mediastinal gland enlargement.
This points to small cell carcinoma, also called oat-cell carcinoma, a highly malignant cancer that most often arises in the lung.
Compared with non-small cell cancer, it has a shorter doubling time, a higher growth fraction, and earlier metastases.
It is often associated with ectopic hormone production and paraneoplastic syndromes.
